task_description:
# Repair Progressive Enhancement for a Qwik City Ticket Form

## Background
A Qwik City (v1.20.0, `@builder.io/qwik` + `@builder.io/qwik-city`) application at `/home/user/project` renders a support-ticket page at the route `/`. The page lists existing tickets (loaded on the server) and provides a form to create a new ticket. The form is meant to be *progressively enhanced*: it must behave correctly BOTH when JavaScript is disabled (the browser performs a native full-page POST and the server renders the result) AND when JavaScript is enabled (the submission is handled on the client with no full-page reload, an in-flight running state, and live validation errors).

The current implementation is broken. With JavaScript disabled, submitting the form does nothing. With JavaScript enabled, submissions do not display validation errors, and in both cases the values the user typed are lost when a submission is rejected. Repair the application so that both submission paths work correctly, without changing the route, control names, validation rules, or the exact strings described below.

## Requirements
- The route `/` renders, on the same page:
  - A list of existing tickets. Each ticket displays its title and its priority.
  - A create-ticket form with these controls (exact `name` attributes): `title` (text input), `priority` (a selector whose value is one of `low`, `medium`, `high`), and `description` (multiline text input).
- Submitting a valid form creates a new ticket on the server and adds it to the list.
- Validation runs on the server with these rules and EXACT messages (the message text must appear on the page for the offending field):
  - `title`: at least 3 characters — `Title must be at least 3 characters`.
  - `description`: at least 10 characters — `Description must be at least 10 characters`.
  - `priority`: must be exactly one of `low`, `medium`, `high` — `Priority must be low, medium, or high`.
- On a REJECTED submission, the page shows the relevant field message(s) AND preserves the values the user already entered for `title`, `description`, and `priority`. No ticket is created.
- On a SUCCESSFUL submission, the page shows the confirmation text `Ticket created: <title>` (with the created ticket's actual title) and the new ticket appears in the list.
- No-JavaScript path: with scripting disabled, submitting performs a native full-page POST to `/`; the server processes it and returns a full HTML page reflecting the outcome (new ticket + confirmation on success, or field messages + preserved values on failure).
- JavaScript-enabled path: with scripting enabled, submitting does NOT cause a full-page navigation. While the submission is in flight, the submit button is disabled and shows the text `Submitting...`; when idle it shows `Create ticket`. After a successful submission the ticket list updates in place to include the new ticket.
- The create action already contains a deliberate ~1 second server-side processing delay (simulating a database write). Keep this delay so that the JS-enabled in-flight running state is observable.
- The initial ticket list must be rendered on the server (present in the initial HTML response before any client JavaScript runs).

## Implementation Hints
- Project path: `/home/user/project`
- Build command: `npm run build`
- Start command: `npm run serve`
- Port: 3000
- Page URL: `http://localhost:3000/`
- The list and the create form MUST live on the same route `/`, and the form MUST submit to `/`.
- Do NOT change the route path, the control `name` attributes (`title`, `priority`, `description`), the allowed `priority` values (`low`, `medium`, `high`), the validation thresholds, or any of the exact message/label strings given above (`Title must be at least 3 characters`, `Description must be at least 10 characters`, `Priority must be low, medium, or high`, `Ticket created: <title>`, `Submitting...`, `Create ticket`).
- Loading `http://localhost:3000/` with JavaScript enabled must not produce any browser console errors.
task_integrations: - None. The application is fully self-contained: Qwik / Qwik City run locally with an in-memory ticket store and a local Node server. No external APIs, databases, cloud services, authentication, or network access are required.

# Verification Plan

## Setup
1. `cd /home/user/project`
2. Build the app: `npm run build`
3. Start the production server: `npm run serve` (must listen on port 3000). Wait until `http://localhost:3000/` responds with HTTP 200.
4. Use a Chromium browser automation tool (Playwright) that can create browser contexts with JavaScript enabled and disabled, and can read the browser console.
5. The server keeps ticket state in memory for the life of the process. Use the distinct ticket titles specified below so checks do not depend on how many tickets already exist; assert only on the presence of the specific titles/messages named in each step.

## Verification Steps

1. **SSR renders the ticket list (server-side loader).**
   - Fetch the raw HTML of `http://localhost:3000/` without executing JavaScript (e.g., `curl`).
   - Expected: the HTML contains the two seeded ticket titles `Set up CI pipeline` and `Write onboarding docs`, and contains a `<form>` with controls named `title`, `priority`, and `description`. The idle submit control shows `Create ticket`.

2. **No-JS successful submit performs a native full-page POST and creates the ticket.**
   - Open a browser context with JavaScript DISABLED; navigate to `http://localhost:3000/`.
   - Fill `title` = `Fix login redirect`, set `priority` = `high`, `description` = `Users bounce back to the login page after signing in`.
   - Submit the form (a full-page navigation is expected).
   - Expected: the resulting document contains `Ticket created: Fix login redirect`, and the rendered ticket list contains `Fix login redirect`.

3. **No-JS rejected submit shows messages and preserves entered values.**
   - JavaScript DISABLED; navigate to `http://localhost:3000/`.
   - Fill `title` = `Hi`, set `priority` = `medium`, `description` = `too short`.
   - Submit the form.
   - Expected: after the full-page POST, the page contains BOTH `Title must be at least 3 characters` and `Description must be at least 10 characters`; the `title` input's value is still `Hi`, the `description` input's value is still `too short`, and the `priority` selector's value is still `medium`. The list does NOT contain a ticket titled `Hi`.

4. **JS-enhanced successful submit updates the list without navigation and toggles the running state.**
   - Open a browser context with JavaScript ENABLED; start capturing console messages; navigate to `http://localhost:3000/`.
   - Expected on load: no console errors were emitted.
   - Fill `title` = `Add dark mode`, set `priority` = `low`, `description` = `Provide a dark theme toggle in settings`.
   - Click the submit control and immediately observe it: the control becomes disabled and its text is `Submitting...` while the request is in flight.
   - Expected after completion: NO full-page navigation occurred (the document was not reloaded); the page shows `Ticket created: Add dark mode`; the ticket list now contains `Add dark mode`; the submit control is enabled again and shows `Create ticket`.
   - To prove no reload occurred: before clicking submit, set a sentinel on the window (e.g., `window.__noReload = true` via `page.evaluate`); after completion, confirm the sentinel is still present.

5. **JS-enhanced rejected submit shows messages, preserves values, and does not navigate.**
   - JavaScript ENABLED; set the `window.__noReload` sentinel; navigate to `http://localhost:3000/`.
   - Fill `title` = `ok`, set `priority` = `high`, `description` = `nope`.
   - Click the submit control.
   - Expected: no full-page navigation (sentinel still present); the page shows BOTH `Title must be at least 3 characters` and `Description must be at least 10 characters`; the `title` input still holds `ok`, the `description` input still holds `nope`, and the `priority` selector still holds `high`. No ticket titled `ok` appears in the list.

6. **Server-side priority enum validation (anti-cheat: not enforced only by the UI).**
   - GET `http://localhost:3000/` and read the `action` attribute of the create `<form>` (the URL the form posts to).
   - Send an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` POST to that exact URL with `title=Valid title`, `priority=urgent`, `description=this description is long enough`.
   - Expected: the response body contains `Priority must be low, medium, or high`, and no ticket titled `Valid title` is added to the list (verified by a subsequent GET of `http://localhost:3000/`).
